why: Every UPDATE and ALL row-level-security policy in the live public schema, as pg_policies reports it. tests/rls-update-check.test.mjs holds it to the rule that migrations/ is held to: a policy a client role can use states its WITH CHECK, and that check keeps every owner column its USING names. Postgres reuses USING when WITH CHECK is absent, so a NULL with_check is not an open hole by itself, but it reads as one and it ties the write check to whatever USING later becomes (scorecard §3 #17, 2026-09-28).
refresh: Supabase connector execute_sql: select json_agg(json_build_object('table', tablename, 'policy', policyname, 'cmd', cmd, 'permissive', permissive, 'roles', roles, 'using', qual, 'check', with_check) order by tablename, policyname) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'public' and cmd in ('UPDATE', 'ALL'); -- paste the array into policies, one policy per line, and move dumpedAt. Refresh only AFTER a migration is applied: the snapshot is what production has, not what a migration file intends.
